name: Comparing to the dash with char equality (charAt == '-') vs reference equality on Strings (substring(...) == "-")
side_a: If the answer tests for the hyphen using a primitive char comparison (e.g. `username.charAt(i + 1) == '-'`), where `==` is the semantically correct operator, give credit for the comparison even if indices/loop bounds are off.
side_b: If the answer compares String objects with `==` (e.g. `username.substring(i + 1, i + 2) == "-"`) instead of `.equals("-")`, withhold credit: the condition is a reference comparison that does not reliably detect the hyphen, so the separator is never recognized.

name: Indexing past the end of the string (unguarded `charAt(i + 1)` / `i <= length()`) counts as a disqualifying bounds error vs. is forgiven as an edge-case slip
side_a: no_deduct: if the pieces of the string being concatenated and returned are the right ones, ignore the fact that the index used to inspect/extract a character can run one past the last valid index (e.g., `charAt(i + 1)` on the final character, or a loop bounded by `i <= username.length()`); treat it as a harmless edge-case slip since the intended construction is clear.
side_b: deduct: an index expression that can reach `length()` or beyond — `username.charAt(i + 1)` with no guard that `i + 1 < username.length()`, or a loop condition `i <= username.length()` — is a genuine out-of-bounds/bounds error, so the method throws instead of returning the shortened string and B3 is lost.

name: Comparing substrings with `==` treated as an excused String-API misuse vs. as a wrong-logic comparison
side_a: no_deduct: comparing one-character substrings with `==` instead of `.equals` is just another instance of using a String method/operator incorrectly; if the intended selection and concatenation of characters is right, give the point.
side_b: deduct: `username.substring(i + 1, i + 2) == "-"` tests reference identity, so the hyphen is never detected and the method returns the unshortened name; this is a logic error in the algorithm, not an excused String-method call, and B3 is lost.
